content.overview: Shift handoff transfers factual work status, open risks and next actions so cultivation operations remain continuous even when individual workers leave.

vocabulary.definition: A structured transfer of work status, risk, observations and priorities from one worker or shift to another.
A task, deviation, alarm, hold or decision that remains unresolved at handoff.
Communication in which receipt is confirmed and responsibility for the next action is clear.

sections.title: Make unresolved work visible
sections.body: The next shift needs to know what was completed, what remains incomplete, what changed, what is on hold, which alarms or deviations exist and which tasks are time-sensitive. Handoffs should not hide risk beneath a list of routine completed work.

sections.title: Use precise, bounded language
sections.body: A useful handoff identifies the room, asset, plant or batch, factual observation, status, person notified and next action. It separates observation from unsupported diagnosis and does not imply an issue is closed merely because it was mentioned.

workedExamples: A held batch is handed off with exact identifier, location, reason, person notified and next authorized action.
An irrigation issue is described by the affected zone and observed no-flow condition rather than as 'irrigation broken everywhere.'
commonMistakes: Omitting unresolved risks while listing routine completed work.
Using vague descriptions without identifiers, locations or next actions.
content.practicalApplication: Write an end-of-shift handoff from a packet containing completed tasks, a traceability discrepancy, an equipment fault, a biosecurity hold and routine observations.
content.summary: A strong handoff keeps work, risk and responsibility visible across shifts through precise identifiers, factual status, open items and clear next actions.
